key_insight: MobileMoE introduces an on-device MoE scaling law and a family of sub-billion active-parameter MoE models that achieve superior accuracy vs. latency/memory trade-offs, establishing a new Pareto frontier for on-device LLMs.
problem_solved: Current MoE architectures are optimized for very large server models and have not been tuned for strict on-device constraints (latency, memory, compute). This work addresses how to scale and configure MoE so high-capability language models can run efficiently on mobile/edge devices.
method: Formulate an on-device MoE scaling law that jointly optimizes model width, number of experts, and routing for device latency and memory budgets.
Design the MobileMoE family with 0.3–0.9B active parameters (1.3–5.3B total) to maximize performance under on-device constraints and identify Pareto-optimal points.
Apply system-aware optimizations (efficient routing, quantization-friendly layouts and runtime-aware parameter allocation) to enable practical on-device deployment.
impact: Provides practitioners a principled recipe to build efficient, high-quality LLMs for mobile/edge environments — enabling lower latency, better privacy, and broader offline capabilities without sacrificing model capability.
visual_elements: Pareto frontier plot: accuracy (y) vs. latency or memory (x) showing MobileMoE models dominating existing on-device LLMs
Architecture diagram: Mixture-of-Experts block with router, active experts highlighted and parameter split (active vs total)
Scaling-law illustration: trade-off curves for expert count, width, and device constraints guiding model selection
Bar/stacked chart: active parameters vs. total parameters and corresponding memory footprint for representative MobileMoE sizes
paper_title: MobileMoE: Scaling On-Device Mixture of Experts
paper_authors: Yanbei Chen, Hanxian Huang, Ernie Chang, Jacob Szwejbka, Digant Desai
